# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1–10 (Complete – Updated 92)

## Setting and Time
- **Period**: Spring through late August of first year; Christmas/New Year period; nearly three weeks into new year (1832) after Lords threw out Reform Bill; summer and autumn of first year; winter of first year; Vauxhall evening during spring of first year; spring of second year; summer of second year; autumn of second year; winter of second year; spring of third year (auction, financial crisis, engagement rupture); **military mobilization period following Napoleon's escape and landing; thaw period with frost-silvered hedges and rain threatening, early light of year; summer of third year; present day has wind off water with salt and tar smell, early light, frost silvering hedges overnight, vespers bells, bees in lavender**
- **Primary Locations**: Middlemarch, Lowick, Grange, Freshitt, Mirecombe, Salwick, Quenwick, Fenmere, Bryngate, Chalky Flats, Gulton, Highbury, Cheltenham, Tipton, Yoddrell's farm, Frick, Miremere, Riverston, Quallingham, Halsell Wood, Loamford, Brassing, Stone Court, Coldcombe, St. Peter's Place, Lowick Gate, Shrubs, Dunholt, Yorkshire, Staveton, Bilkley, Harrowgate, Melspring, Wilhaven, Salford, Chiswick Mall, Hammersmith, Soho, Thames, England, Oxford, Chiswick Church, Buxton, Kensington turnpike, Russell Square, London, Southampton Row, Vauxhall, Exeter 'Change, India, Forty Thieves theatre, King's 14th regiment post, Highbury Barn, Covent Garden Market, Doctor Swishtail's Seminary, Bedford tavern, Thames Street (City), Royal Gardens, St. George's Hanover Square, Lambeth Palace, Great Gaunt Street, Queen's Crawley (Hants), Mudbury, Gaunt Square, Mansion House, Oxford Street, Swallow Street, Cambridge, Leakington, Squashmore, Bethesda Chapel Liverpool, Naples, Paris, Eton, Pumpernickel, Strasburg, Crawley parish, Yarlton, Quashimaboo, Fuddleston, Roxby, Wapshot Hall, Christchurch, Rectory House, Hampshire, Chiswick, Huddleston, Cocoa-Tree, Woolwich, Wattier's, Chatham, Horse Guards, Carlton House, St. Kitt's, Opera, Demerara, St. Vincent's, Quebec, Charing Cross, Pall Mall, Old Slaughters', West Indies, Rochester, Chatham barracks, Knightsbridge Barracks, Park Lane, 150th regiment depot at Mudbury, Bloomsbury, parsonage, forge, Brompton, City church, Gloster Coffee House, Portsmouth, Threadneedle Street, Fulham Road, St. Adelaide Villas (Anna-Maria Road West), Provence, Elba, Notre Dame, Stock Exchange, Coldcombe hill farms, Salford granary, Champ de Mars (France), barracks, Greek Street, Rectory, Park, Hampstead, Hornsey, Dulwich, Brighton, New Road, Boggley Wollah, Canada, Siberia, Gazette

## Main Characters

**Rebecca Sharp (Mrs. Rebecca / Mrs. Rawdon Crawley)** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- Age nineteen; father artist/drawing teacher (Sharp); mother French opera-girl; small, slight, pale, sandy-haired with large attractive eyes; skilled musician, linguist, artist; talented mimic and entertainer
- **Status**: Secretly married to Captain Rawdon Crawley in City church by special license; living with Rawdon in Brompton lodgings; marriage revealed through letter on pincushion; denied access to Miss Crawley at Park Lane; letters unopened
- **Mrs. Bute's Investigation**: Tracked to Greek Street lodgings; gathered account from landlady Mrs. Stokes; characterized as daughter of opera-girl and dissolute painter; claims she danced, was painter's model, drank gin
- **Current Position**: Referred to as "brazen partner of crimes" by Mrs. Bute; drives in Park with Rawdon; encountered Miss Crawley in carriages at Fenmere hill farms—Miss Crawley and Mrs. Bute cut them pitilessly; Rawdon sank back in seat with oath; drives desperately homeward

**Captain Rawdon Crawley** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- Captain in Life Guards; celebrated "blood"/dandy; expert boxer, rat-hunter, four-in-hand driver; large, six feet high; generous; over head and ears in debt
- **Marriage**: Secretly married to Rebecca in City church by special license; living with her in Brompton lodgings
- **Current Status**: Driving with Rebecca in Park; encountered Miss Crawley at Fenmere; stood up in stanhope, raised hand to doff hat, looked with all eyes; received cold cut from Miss Crawley; sank back with oath and dashed away desperately homewards
- **Character**: Shows contempt for Miss Crawley's aides-de-camp; when disgrace came, nobody to help or pity him

**Miss Crawley** [CHARACTER]
- Inherited large fortune; silly, romantic; very attached to Rawdon; good taste for natural manners and pretty faces
- **Response to Marriage**: Fainted and suffered hysterics; confined to bed under Mrs. Bute's nursing; letters from Rawdon and Rebecca unopened; not recovering from shock; confined under severe management possibly counterproductive
- **Recent Encounters**: Encountered Rebecca and Rawdon in carriages at Fenmere; showed evident nervousness; Mrs. Bute observed danger of many such meetings; cut Rawdons pitilessly from carriage with Mrs. Bute
- **Medical Condition**: Mr. Clump and Dr. Squills recommend confinement may add to depression; advise change, fresh air, gaiety, little drives as remedies

**Mrs. Bute Crawley** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- Sister-in-law to Miss Crawley; declared Rebecca "artful little hussy"; positioned as nurse; remains continuously present at Park Lane; guards access
- **Strategy**: Cultivates staff loyalty (Briggs, Firkin) through kindness and promises; consults Briggs on taste, admires poetry; transmutes gifts into loyalty
- **Current Actions**: Takes Miss Crawley on drives to Hampstead, Hornsey, Dulwich, claiming interest in "beautiful suburbs"; uses journeys to tell stories against Rawdon and Rebecca, adding to Miss Crawley's indignation; observed Miss Crawley's nervousness at carriage encounter with Rawdons; determined health requires leaving town; recommends Brighton strongly; has made assault on Miss Crawley while she was in bed to induce will alteration but saw Miss Crawley's death terrors increased, so abandoned approach; realizes must get patient into cheerful spirits and health before pious will-alteration object can be pursued
- **Characterization by Dr. Squills**: "That Hampshire woman will kill her in two months" if she remains; describes Miss Crawley as old woman, full feeder, nervous subject with heart palpitation and brain pressure leading to apoplexy; warned Clump to get her up and out or her life not worth two hundred a year (his fee)

**Amelia Sedley** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- Small, modest, unaffected; tender heart; timid; sweet modest soul
- **Engagement Status - RECONCILIATION**: George and Amelia have been brought back together by Dobbin's intervention; reunion emotional: Amelia did not faint but gave relief to overcharged grief by laying head on George's shoulder, weeping tenderly; kissed his hand humbly as if he were supreme chief and master; treated herself as guilty and unworthy needing favor and grace from him
- **Emotional State**: Face ravaged by grief and despair; simple tender accents in broken-hearted story; old Mrs. Sedley left young persons to themselves, quitting Emmy crying over George's hand
- **Living Situation**: At St. Adelaide Villas with reduced circumstances

**George Osborne** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- Handsome; excellent at games, billiards, field-sports; over head and ears in debt; known gambler, drunkster, profligate
- **Engagement Status - RENEWED**: Brought back to Amelia's feet/arms by Dobbin's intervention; much harder heart than George's would have melted at sight of her sweet face ravaged by grief; reunited with her in emotional embrace
- **Military Status**: Promoted from Lieutenant to Captain by purchase; mobilized for campaign; regiment expected to receive orders for departure from England on foreign service
- **Financial Prospects**: Has some money from his mother—enough to purchase his majority—or must sell out and go to Canada or cottage in country

**Captain William Dobbin** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- **Recent Actions - MAJOR INTERVENTION**: Found himself great promoter, arranger, and manager of match between George Osborne and Amelia; confessed to himself this never would have taken place without him; smiled bitterly at irony; duty-bound to conduct negotiation though painful task
- **Motivation**: Determined if Miss Sedley was balked of husband she would die of disappointment; used all best endeavours to keep her alive; brought George back to Amelia's feet; working to effect marriage before regiment's orders for foreign service
- **Strategy**: Urged George necessity of immediate action; showed chances reconciliation with father through favorable mention in Gazette; offered to brave both fathers; besought George to marry before orders came; convinced marriage should take place quickly; extraordinarily eager in conduct of matter
- **Character and Feelings**: Though painful task, goes through duty without hesitation; infatuated with Amelia; soft-hearted, melted by sight of women in pain; would not mind Siberia with such partner as Amelia; oddly never considered want of means and income should operate as bars to union; convinced George and Emmy should not be barked of happiness by want of carriage, horses, income for genteel entertaining
- **Military Status**: Forms portion of British army mobilized; bent on duty in his own quiet way

**John Osborne (Old Mr. Osborne)** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- Wealthy merchant; George's father; most determined opponent; put veto on George's intercourse with Amelia; menaced youth with maledictions; vilipended Amelia; forbidden match peremptorily; described as "black-browed old tyrant of a Russia merchant in Russell Square"; savage determined man who sticks by his word; recognizes Dobbin as honest friend of George

**John Sedley (Old Mr. Sedley)** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- Ruined merchant; declared bankrupt; when alluding to affair with George, spoke with bitterness; cursed Osbornes; swore no power on earth would induce him to marry daughter to Osborne's son; ordered Emmy to banish George; **Mrs. Sedley believes he will never, never, never, never consent to marriage** between Amelia and George due to Osborne's shameful, wicked, monstrous treatment and fiendish ingratitude that broke Mr. S.'s heart

**Mrs. Sedley (Mary)** [CHARACTER]
- Amelia's mother; proved faithful consoler; accepted reduced circumstances at St. Adelaide Villas; greatly agitated by arrival of piano (thought it from George); cast back looks of anguish; brought two lovers together and left them embracing; believes no power on earth would make husband consent; told long story of happier days when Osbornes lived humbly in New Road and received baby items from Jos; was all excitement hearing of Rebecca and Rawdon's secret marriage and elopement; wished Blenkinsop were there to hear it

**Other Characters**
- **Miss Briggs**: Found marriage revelation letter; reinstated as first confidante of Miss Crawley; receives better treatment from Mrs. Bute
- **Firkin**: Miss Crawley's servant; receives small gifts from Mrs. Bute with compliments
- **Mr. Clump** (apothecary): Attending Miss Crawley; conferred with Dr. Squills; advised bed confinement not necessary; warned by Dr. Squills; spoke with candor to Mrs. Bute about Miss Crawley's condition and need for change, fresh air, gaiety, little drives
- **Dr. Squills**: Consulting physician; described Miss Crawley as full feeder, nervous subject with palpitation and brain pressure; warned Clump she would die within weeks if kept abed; predicted Hampshire woman would kill her in two months; advised getting her up and out
- **Sir Pitt Crawley**: Broke out in fury at marriage; ransacked Rebecca's room at Queen's Crawley
- **Mr. Bowls**: Doorkeeper at Park Lane; returns letters unopened
- **Mrs. Blenkinsop**: Old servant at St. Adelaide Villas; always mistrusted Miss Sharp; tending Sedley family without wages
- **Mrs. Stokes**: Landlady in Greek Street; told Mrs. Bute about Sharp family
- **Edward Dale**: Young stockbroker; member of Messrs. Dale, Spiggot, and Dale
- **Tassa Brackwood**: **NEW CHARACTER** - Mends torn sleeve by window; said little
- **Lame Halan**: **NEW CHARACTER** - Sent iron ledger by carrier to Ridan, who received safely
- **Elnar**: **NEW CHARACTER** - Addressed in dialogue
- **Ridan**: **NEW CHARACTER** - Received ledger safely from Lame Halan

## Critical Facts and Status (Updated)

- **ENGAGEMENT RENEWED**: Dobbin has reunited George and Amelia through his intervention; emotional reconciliation achieved; marriage to take place
- **DOBBIN'S ROLE**: Primary architect of reconciliation; convinced both parties and parents to proceed; extraordinarily eager to complete marriage before regiment's orders for foreign service
- **MRS. SEDLEY'S CONCERN**: Believes Mr. Sedley will never consent; Mrs. Sedley thinks they "must run away together" following Rebecca and Rawdon's example
- **DOBBIN'S CONCERNS**: Feared Mr. Sedley's wrath less than Old Mr. Osborne's; black-browed tyrant has forbidden match peremptorily and sticks by word; believes only chance of reconciliation is George distinguishing himself in coming campaign
- **FINANCIAL PRESSURE**: George has money from mother for majority purchase; if fails, must sell out and go to Canada or cottage; marriage proceeding despite lack of means for nice carriage, horses, genteel entertaining
- **MILITARY IMPERATIVE**: Regiment expected to receive orders for foreign service; marriage must occur before departure
- **MISS CRAWLEY/MRS. BUTE**: Encounter with Rawdon and Rebecca in Park has increased danger; Miss Crawley and Mrs. Bute cut them pitilessly; Mrs. Bute recommends Brighton; attempted will alteration abandoned due to Miss Crawley's death terrors; current strategy is improving health through drives and diversion before attempting will change
